questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of cohort analysis?

options.text: To segment users by demographic attributes
To track the behavior of a group of users over time
To calculate lifetime value of individual users
To predict future revenue using machine learning

questions.explanation: Cohort analysis focuses on groups of users sharing a characteristic and observing their behavior across time periods.

questions.prompt: In a cohort analysis, how is the retention rate for a cohort typically calculated?

options.text: Number of new users in the cohort / total users
Number of active users in a later period / number of users in the initial period
Total revenue / number of cohorts
Average session duration / number of sessions

questions.explanation: Retention rate compares users still active in a later period to the original cohort size.

questions.prompt: Which statement best differentiates cohort analysis from simple segmentation?

options.text: Cohort analysis groups users by device type, segmentation does not
Cohort analysis tracks changes over time, segmentation is static
Segmentation uses machine learning, cohort analysis uses rule-based filters
Segmentation is only for marketing, cohort analysis is only for product

questions.explanation: Cohort analysis examines how a group’s behavior evolves, whereas segmentation only categorizes users at a point in time.

questions.prompt: Which metric would you look at in cohort analysis to identify a sudden increase in churn?

options.text: Average order value
Cohort retention drop between two consecutive months
Total number of new users
User acquisition cost

questions.explanation: A sharp decline in retention between periods signals higher churn for that cohort.

questions.prompt: When would cohort analysis provide more insight than a simple time‑series trend chart?

options.text: When you only care about overall revenue growth
When you want to compare the behavior of users who joined in different months
When you need to forecast next quarter sales
When you are analyzing daily active users

questions.explanation: Cohort analysis reveals differences between groups that a single trend line cannot show.

questions.prompt: A product manager wants to know if users who signed up in January stay active longer than those who signed up in February. Which analysis should they perform?

options.text: A cohort analysis comparing January vs February cohorts
A segment analysis by signup month
A churn prediction model
A cohort analysis of revenue per cohort

questions.explanation: Comparing January and February cohorts tracks retention over time for each signup group.
